heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 Mini can extrude Polymaker PolyLite ABS at speeds up to 214 mm/s backed by an 18 mm³/s volumetric flow limit, but its open-frame design severely restricts print size due to thermal warping. Successful prints require setting the bed to its hardware maximum of 80°C alongside a dedicated draft shield or tent enclosure.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with Liquid Glue / PVP Glue Stick as an adhesion promoter and release agent
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 18 mm³/s under the Filament > Advanced tab to avoid extruder skipping at 255°C.
Enable a Draft Shield (Auto or Full Height) under Others > Draft Shield to trap heat on the open bed.
Set Bed Temperature to the hardware ceiling of 80°C for all layers and lower Part Cooling Fan to 0% for standard layers (max 15% for bridges/overhangs).
Configure a 5-8mm Outer Brim with a 0.0mm Brim-object gap to counteract extreme corner lifting on the 80°C bed.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe bed warping and corner lifting
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The A1 Mini bed maxes out at 80°C, which is below PolyLite ABS's glass transition temperature (Tg ~100°C), exacerbated by open-air ambient drafts.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply PVP glue stick to the Textured PEI plate, add an 8mm mouse-ear or full brim with 0.0mm gap, and cover the printer with a passive draft enclosure.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive cooling from ambient air currents and part cooling fan freezing extruded layers before molecular bonding occurs.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Set part cooling fan threshold to 0% minimum and 15% maximum, increase nozzle temperature to 260°C, and enable an OrcaSlicer draft shield.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Extruder clicking and under-extrusion at high speeds
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Exceeding the melt capacity of the stock stainless steel hotend when attempting to print beyond 18 mm³/s.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Clamp maximum volumetric flow rate to 18 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer and ensure print speeds do not surpass 214 mm/s for 0.2mm layer heights.

faq.question: Can the Bambu Lab A1 Mini print large ABS parts reliably?
faq.answer: No. Due to the bed temperature limit of 80°C and lack of a heated chamber, prints with footprints larger than 50-70mm will inevitably warp or crack without a draft-free enclosure.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle for PolyLite ABS?
faq.answer: No. Standard PolyLite ABS is non-abrasive, meaning the stock stainless steel nozzle on the A1 Mini is fully compatible and will not suffer premature wear.

faq.question: Can I put the A1 Mini inside a sealed thermal enclosure?
faq.answer: Caution is required. The A1 Mini has motherboard and power supply electronics mounted directly on the frame; ambient enclosure temps should not exceed 45°C to avoid thermal runaway or electronics failure.

faq.question: Does Polymaker PolyLite ABS need drying before printing?
faq.answer: Yes. ABS is hygroscopic and absorbs ambient moisture, resulting in stringing, popping at the nozzle, and reduced layer strength. Dry at 65-70°C for at least 6 hours prior to printing.
